name: Whitening mouthwash
lead: Whitening mouthwashes are rinses, some containing hydrogen peroxide and others non-peroxide agents, sold to lighten teeth or reduce staining with daily use. Listerine Whitening is one product examined in laboratory research.[1]

Wikipedia describes rinses as used twice daily for one minute, with visible results possibly taking up to three months, and in the EU retail products may contain up to 0.1% hydrogen peroxide.[2] Contact time is short compared with strips or trays.
Published work found for this entry is mainly in vitro, on enamel, dentine, resin composite and ceramic. No clinical studies were identified.

paras: An in vitro study assessed whether a hydrogen-peroxide-based mouthwash alters enamel colour,[3] and another evaluated non-peroxide mouthrinses for whitening.[4] A laboratory study tested a charcoal-containing toothpaste and mouthwash on stained canines over a simulated 90 days.[5]

Laboratory studies have examined alcohol-containing mouthwashes including Listerine Whitening on enamel and restorative materials,[1] dentine erosion combined with brushing abrasion,[6] and surface hardness and colour stability of resin composite.[7] Another examined bleaching mouthwash and force decay of orthodontic elastomeric chains.[8] Findings are not reproduced here.
No studies found. The related research above is laboratory-based.

card.summary: Daily peroxide or non-peroxide rinses sold to whiten; research so far is lab-based.
card.note: Slow, short contact time; lab studies only.

quick.overview:
Whitening mouthwashes are rinses marketed to lighten teeth with regular use.

Published research is laboratory-based; no clinical studies were found, and sources describe results as slow.
quick.mechanism: Some contain low-level hydrogen peroxide, others non-peroxide agents; they act through brief contact with the teeth during rinsing.
quick.risks: Laboratory studies have examined alcohol-containing rinses for effects on enamel, dentine and restorative materials. EU retail products are limited to 0.1% hydrogen peroxide.
